===== ops/README.md =====
   1: # Operations material
   2: 
   3: Evidence packs and artefacts for working on this service the way you would in
   4: production. Nothing here runs as part of the application or its tests.
   5: 
   6: | Folder | What it holds |
   7: | --- | --- |
   8: | `incidents/INC-2041` | Approvals slow and failing. Logs, metrics and the deploy diff for a completed incident window. |
   9: | `incidents/INC-2047` | Approved invoices not triggering notifications. A live incident, read-only output only. |
  10: | `pipeline` | The service's full CI pipeline and per-step timings for the last 20 runs. |
  11: | `evals` | Ten fixed review cases and a results template. |
  12: 
  13: ## A note on the scenario
  14: 
  15: The invoice approval service in this repository is an internal tool. The
  16: material here assumes the version of it that is going to production: a
  17: 24x7 on-call rotation, a database, a message topic, and an integration with
  18: an external payment provider called PayEx. None of that is in the code yet,
  19: which is the point â€” the diagrams, decisions and policies have to be made
  20: before it is.
  21: 
  22: Names, hosts and figures are invented. No real system, customer or vendor
  23: appears anywhere in this folder.
  24: 
  25: ## No answers here
  26: 
  27: These packs deliberately do not state what the root cause is, which cases
  28: contain defects, or which pipeline changes are safe. Working that out is the
  29: exercise. If you are facilitating rather than participating, the answers are
  30: in the session runbook, not in the repository.

===== ops/incidents/INC-2041/README.md =====
   1: # INC-2041 â€” Approvals slow and failing
   2: 
   3: Evidence pack for the invoice approval service, 14 January 2026.
   4: 
   5: ## What you have
   6: 
   7: | File | What it is |
   8: | --- | --- |
   9: | `alert.md` | The alert that fired, and what the on-call engineer knew at the time |
  10: | `app-logs.txt` | Application log export, 09:40Z to 11:10Z, levels INFO / WARN / ERROR |
  11: | `metrics.csv` | Per-minute platform metrics across the same window |
  12: | `deploy-diff.patch` | The diff for the release that went out that morning |
  13: 
  14: ## How to use it
  15: 
  16: This pack is for analysis, not for fixing. Work out what happened and what you
  17: would check next. The evidence is complete enough to support a ranked set of
  18: hypotheses and to rule some out.
  19: 
  20: Nothing in these files states a conclusion. If you think you have found one,
  21: the test is whether you can point at the lines that support it, and name what
  22: you would look at to prove yourself wrong.
  23: 
  24: ## Context you would have had on the day
  25: 
  26: - Release 2.14.0 was deployed that morning. The previous release, 2.13.4, had
  27:   been running for nine days without incident.
  28: - 14 January is the second-to-last working day of the month, which is the
  29:   heaviest approval window of the cycle.
  30: - PayEx is an external payment provider. The invoice approval service calls it
  31:   over HTTPS. PayEx reported no incident on their status page that day.
  32: - The service runs on three instances behind a load balancer.
